summary.intent: Finish the F2 work package (release-PR decisions from the version plan) by getting lint/tests/CI steps passing, pushing, linking it to trail #457 and updating PR #567, then merge F1/F2 into the G worktree and start designing `.changeset/pre/` handling.
summary.outcome: F2 passed `just test`, lint was fixed with a `ConsumedCase` type alias, and it was pushed and linked to trail #457, with the PR #567 title and body updated. Accidentally committed `mutants.out.old/` was removed from F2 and from G after the merges, and the remaining `ci` steps were run in F1. G's `.changeset/pre/` design had only reached the exploratory grep stage.

repo: `just ci` runs lint, test, doc-check, zizmor, workflow-contracts, release-workflow-behavior and coverage (90) in sequence. A background run can stop after `test`, so later steps have to be run explicitly.
Clippy's complex-type lint applies to test code too, so large tuple types in tests need a named type alias (e.g. `ConsumedCase`).
`deny.toml` is owned by WP A. A RUSTSEC advisory seen in F2/F1 was flagged to the lead session instead of being fixed locally.
Work packages live in separate git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/wp-*`, with branches named `worktree-wp-*`. Merging them into another worktree can carry over stray committed files.
Commits are expected to be signed, and `gh api ...commit.verification.reason` is used to check that.
`cargo-mutants` output (`mutants.out`, `mutants.out.old`) is not gitignored, so `git add -A` can commit it. Only F2 had it committed; F1 was clean.

code.finding: The test `a_version_commit_deletes_exactly...` declared `cases` as a complex tuple array type, which clippy rejected. It was replaced with a `ConsumedCase` alias.

workflow: Run `just lint` before pushing; here it caught an issue that `just test` did not.
After merging branches, check for stray artifacts such as mutants output with `git ls-tree` or `git ls-files`, and delete the local copies so later `git add -A` calls can't re-add them.
Use `git rm --cached` plus a signed commit to untrack accidentally committed generated output, then delete the local copy.
Keep PR descriptions in a file and apply them with `gh pr edit --body-file`.
Use `entire trail link` and `entire trail ci-pr` to attach a branch to a trail.
Cross-session coordination goes through SendMessage, e.g. replying to the lead and flagging advisories.
